title: Choosing between array, unordered_map and map
summary: A decision rule for picking the counting/lookup container, with speed, order and key-type trade-offs.

sections.title: The rule
sections.body:
✍️ Keys are small integers in a known range (letters, digits, values ≤ 10⁶) → **plain array** (`int cnt[26]`, `vector<int> cnt(maxV+1)`). Fastest, O(1) true worst case.
✍️ Keys are arbitrary (large ints, strings), order does not matter → **unordered_map / unordered_set**. O(1) average.
✍️ You need sorted order, min/max, or lower_bound → **map / set**. O(log n).
✍️ Keys are pairs or vectors and you do not want to write a hash → **map**.

sections.title: Side by side
sections.body:
| | array | unordered_map | map |
|---|---|---|---|
| lookup | O(1) | O(1) avg, O(n) worst | O(log n) |
| ordered iteration | yes (by index) | no | yes |
| memory | size of range | ~3–5× entries | ~3× entries |
| key types | small ints | hashable | comparable |

sections.title: Example: Valid Anagram
sections.body:
✍️ Lowercase letters only → `int cnt[26]`: increment for s, decrement for t, check all zero.
- If the problem allowed Unicode, the range would not be small → `unordered_map<char,int>` (the official follow-up of LeetCode 242).
